title: Crispy air fryer tofu bowl
summary: The cornstarch coating is the whole trick - it is the difference between crisp cubes and sad grey ones. Vegan, 28 g of protein.

time.note: Most of the prep time is pressing the tofu, which is hands-off.

ingredients.note: Silken or soft tofu will not work here at all.
Balances the salt in the glaze - a teaspoon of any sweetener does the job.

steps: Press the tofu: wrap the block in a clean towel, put a heavy pan on top, leave 15 minutes. Squeezing the water out is what lets it crisp.
Cube it into 2 cm pieces. Toss gently with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce and the sesame oil, then dust over the cornstarch and toss again until every face is chalky and dry-looking.
Air fry at 200C / 400F for 15-18 minutes, shaking the basket twice. Single layer, always.
While it cooks, stir the remaining soy sauce, garlic, ginger, sweetener, vinegar and chilli flakes together in a small bowl.
Tip the hot tofu straight into the sauce and toss for a few seconds only. Any longer and the crust softens.
Serve over rice with the broccoli, scattered with spring onion and sesame.
tips: Do not sauce it in advance. Crisp tofu plus wet sauce equals soggy tofu within minutes - combine at the table if you are packing it for lunch.
No air fryer: 220C oven on a lined tray for 25-30 minutes, turning once. Or a hot pan with a tablespoon of oil, undisturbed for 3 minutes a side.
Freeze and thaw the tofu block first if you want a chewier, spongier texture that soaks up more sauce.
health_notes: Tofu is a complete protein at roughly 15 g per 100 g. Cornstarch is what crisps it, so this needs a fraction of the oil deep-frying would.

source.adapted: Common cornstarch-crisping method, moved to the air fryer to cut the oil right down.
